lines.t: Hear the summit? First time in weeks the whole mountain's been humming. My bowl's ringing along with it.
Rest your troupe? The fire's hotter when the stones sing. Probably. I'm not a scientist.

options.label: Help a kin recall a move

lines.t: Cold up here steals strength. The bowl gives it back. Mind the ice outside.
Rest your troupe? Open the Fosterage ledger? Or just thawing your fingers?

options.label: Help a kin recall a move

lines.t: Lodge Chandlery! Salves, Chimes, and one very good scarf that is not for sale. It's mine. I'm wearing it.
There. It'll stay frozen for good — stairs all the way up. Catch a frost friend when you can; the glacier's full of them.
Falls won't hold weight unless a frost voice sings them solid. Need a hand?
Any frost kin in your troupe can do it — even a sleepy one. If you've none, I'll lend you my Rimelet. Just this once.
Twenty years guiding folk up Hoarcrown and I've never heard the summit this loud. It's showing off. Good for it.
You froze the falls! Now everyone wants to climb. I'll need a bigger hat to look important in.
Rime Hall sits on the west terrace. The summit path's north — but there's a big fellow in a brass helmet parked on it.
Welcome to Hoarcrown! Lodge is east, falls are north, and the summit is… up. Mostly up.
Folk in slate coats hauled a bell past here on a sledge. A bell! Up a mountain! Nobody hauls a bell for fun.
The falls only turn to stairs for a frost voice. Plenty of frosty kin on the glacier if you've none of your own.
My ice blocks are humming. I cut them, I stack them, and now they sing at me. Business is weird today.
I cut ice for the lodge. Best ice comes from the terraces — the rime here remembers every note it's heard.
Lately it's been remembering nothing. Very quiet ice. Makes me nervous. Ice shouldn't be mysterious.
Hear that? Every stone from here to the coast, all at once. Loud. Messy.
…Better than quiet. I'm going back to the quarry. Honest rock. Only sings when you drop it on your foot.
Magister's at the ring. Go on. I'll keep the lads off your back.
Magister's up top. Bell's half on. I'm supposed to stop you.
Six Keynotes, eh? Last time we met, you had a handful and a lot of nerve. Now you've got the whole song.
My miners' kin strayed when their stone went dead. Took you to get them home. I've not forgotten.
…Go on. I've heard enough quiet.
Magister's up top. Bell's half on. I'm supposed to stop you.
And today, I will. You're one Keynote short of anything clever. Rime Hall's on the west terrace.
Come back with the whole song. Then we'll see what I'm supposed to do.
…Why was it *singing*? It shouldn't have — the coils were seated. Every figure was right.
Your {starter} answered the ring. The Chordstone flared, and its own song split the Great Stillbell from rim to crown.
Far below, bell after bell cracks in sympathy. Every stone in Cantarra hums again — loud, bright, a little off-key.
Then no one holds the bell.
…Promise me someone will at least *listen* when a stone starts to shout.

options.label: You could be the one listening.

lines.t: {player}. You climbed. Of course you did. Oriel never could leave a stone alone either.
The Bell is nearly seated. Once it holds, every stone in Cantarra waits for permission. Stand aside.
The Bell is nearly seated. You're early, {player}. And unfinished — I can hear it. Five notes, not six.
{player}! I ran up the whole stair! Every stone on the way down lit up like a birthday! Was that YOU?
Of course it was you. And your {starter}! Look at them, all smug. They've earned smug.
Oriel sent this up with me in case you 'did something foolish and wonderful'. Her words. She was crying a bit.
The lift behind the ring goes to Concord Spire. Mum's up there. So's our last battle. Don't be slow!
Six Keynotes, a singing summit, and a lift. That's the whole recipe. Go on — I'll race you up. I will lose that race.
You're standing in a marked service area. I'm obliged to remove you. Politely.
The bell's in pieces. I'll need a much longer form for this.
Honestly? I joined for the helmet. It's very warm.
Ski patrol tip: if you slide, slide *toward* the lodge. It has soup.
The auroras went grey when the stones went quiet. I'd like my colours back, please.
On clear nights the sky over Hoarcrown ripples like a plucked string. Stay up and see.
Falls won't hold weight unless a frost voice sings them solid. Need a hand?
Magister's up top. Bell's half on. I'm supposed to stop you.
…Go on. I've heard enough quiet.
The Bell is nearly seated. Once it holds, every stone in Cantarra waits for permission. Stand aside.
…Why is it *singing*? It shouldn't— the coils are—
Then no one holds the bell.
You see? Unmanaged, it fails. Go down the mountain, {player}.
…Promise me someone will at least *listen* when a stone starts to shout.
